items.q: What is Ahmad Osman's framing of open-source and local AI?
items.a: Open-source AI is an **optimization problem** and local AI is a **user-experience problem**; both need solving together.

items.q: What model future does he bet on?
items.a: **Small, specialized models** of 1-2B parameters with **another model orchestrating** them.

items.q: Why are modest local GPUs already useful for agents?
items.a: Agents spend most time **waiting on shell commands and tools**, not on tokens per second.
Prefill is **compute-bound** (long prompts slow time to first token); decode is **memory-bandwidth-bound**.

items.q: How should you choose local AI hardware?
items.a: By **your workflow**: context length, dense vs MoE, and **parallel agent requests**, which favour high-bandwidth GPUs with mature software.

items.q: Why not quantize every layer to 4 bits?
items.a: It can **nuke the model**; keep the **layers that matter at higher precision** and compress the rarely used ones.

items.q: Why does he want an inference engine per model per chip?
items.a: General engines take **shortcuts to support every device**; real speed comes from **systems engineering per model and chip**.

items.q: Which numbers should you measure on your own hardware?
items.a: **Time to first token, tokens per second per agent, requests per second and task accuracy.**

items.q: How much should you trust public leaderboards?
items.a: Little: they **disagree wildly** and are **being reward-hacked**, so rely on your own traces and evals.
